adverse_media.status: ongoing - company remains in administration as of 2026-10-21
adverse_media.summary: Greensill Capital (UK) Limited entered administration on 8 March 2021 with liabilities of more than GBP 1.6 billion; administrators Russell Simpson, Christine Laverty and Trevor O'Sullivan of Grant Thornton were appointed, with William Stagg the current officeholder

adverse_media.status: concluded - funds frozen and wound down; investor losses crystallised
adverse_media.summary: Credit Suisse froze USD 10 billion of funds invested in Greensill's financial products on 1 March 2021 after trade credit insurance covering the assets lapsed; a core funding source of Greensill Capital

adverse_media.status: complaint filed; later followed by criminal charges (Dec 2025)
adverse_media.summary: German regulator BaFin closed Greensill Bank AG, the Bremen banking subsidiary of the Greensill group, with immediate effect for customer business and issued a sale and payment ban over impending over-indebtedness; BaFin simultaneously filed a criminal complaint (Strafanzeige) against the bank, confirmed by the Bremen public prosecutor's office

adverse_media.status: pending - charges filed, proceedings under way
adverse_media.summary: German prosecutors brought criminal charges against three unnamed people involved in running Greensill Bank in 2021; they are alleged to have avoided banking regulations

Zurich Insurance, sued in London's High Court by the administrators of Greensill Bank AG, filed a defence and counter-claim (26 Jan 2024) alleging the claims arise out of a 'fraudulent scheme' involving Lex Greensill, Greensill Capital UK, Sanjeev Gupta and three Liberty businesses, alleging deliberate or reckless misrepresentation and non-disclosure including that receivables sold by Liberty to GCUK were not genuine; USD 405 million at stake

The UK Serious Fraud Office has criminally investigated Gupta's GFG Alliance since 2021 for suspected fraud and money laundering in an investigation that includes its financing arrangements with Greensill Capital UK; GFG was Greensill's largest client with USD 5 billion exposure

adverse_media.status: concluded - superseded by disqualification undertaking accepted 2 Jun 2026
adverse_media.summary: The Insolvency Service commenced director disqualification proceedings against Alexander (Lex) Greensill for up to 15 years in respect of his conduct as a director of Greensill Capital (UK) Limited and Greensill Limited

adverse_media.status: resolved in the Secretary of State's favour at interlocutory stage
adverse_media.summary: In re Greensill Capital (UK) Ltd [2026] EWHC 639 (Ch): Mr Greensill's application to strike out (or obtain reverse summary judgment on) the Secretary of State's s.6 Company Directors Disqualification Act 1986 proceedings was refused; the judgment records the Catfoss allegations - from September 2018 alleged dishonest misrepresentations and non-disclosures to trade credit insurers, with insurers refusing approximately USD 4.6 billion of investor claims in GCUK's products - and the Katerra allegations

adverse_media.status: concluded - disqualification undertaking accepted 2 Jun 2026, ban effective 23 Jun 2026
adverse_media.summary: Lex Greensill agreed to a nine-year disqualification (until June 2035) after an Insolvency Service investigation: in late 2020 he caused the companies to enter transactions with Katerra that removed legal protections underpinning the Credit Suisse fund's investment, and caused or allowed USD 440 million received in November 2020 to be used for purposes other than redeeming notes owed to the fund, causing the fund a loss of USD 440 million

adverse_media.status: ongoing - recovery outstanding (administrators still owed ~USD 587.2m by GFG as of Apr 2024)
adverse_media.summary: The government-owned British Business Bank lent Greensill up to USD 400 million without detailed checks; the funds were on-lent to eight Gupta-linked companies and the National Audit Office warned the taxpayer could lose GBP 335 million

output.risk_rationale: HIGH. Greensill Capital (UK) Limited (08126173) is in administration since 8 March 2021 with liabilities exceeding GBP 1.6 billion and has no serving directors; its LEI is lapsed. Its PSC and long-time director, Lex Greensill, accepted a nine-year director disqualification (effective 23 June 2026, until June 2035) following Insolvency Service proceedings for causing transactions that stripped protections from a Credit Suisse fund's Katerra investment and misapplying USD 440 million, and the group faces a USD 405 million fraud counter-claim by Zurich Insurance alleging a fraudulent scheme involving Lex Greensill and GCUK, plus roughly USD 4.6 billion of refused investor claims tied to alleged dishonest misrepresentations to trade credit insurers (Catfoss allegations). The group's German subsidiary Greensill Bank AG was closed by BaFin with a criminal complaint filed in 2021, and three of its managers were criminally charged in December 2025; the SFO's GFG Alliance criminal investigation also covers GCUK financing arrangements. Screening found no sanctions matches on OFAC SDN, the UK Sanctions List or the EU consolidated list, and the only PEP exposures are former domestic PEP connections (Lex Greensill's 2012-2015 Downing Street/Cabinet Office adviser role; former PM David Cameron as an adviser), which together with the disqualification, fraud allegations, insolvency and ongoing criminal proceedings in the group put the entity firmly at high risk.
